page.layout: One column of text, full width, with a centred ornament and a centred heading "COROLLARIA" followed by numbered theses set in italic below; no margin notes; catchword at the foot right.

main_text.head: XXXV.
main_text.p: Quanquàm uni corpori non possit tribui nisi unus proprius motus, communes tamen ei convenire eodem tempore possunt plurimi. Ita rotulæ horologij, quod in peră gestat homo in navi ambulans, moventur motu hominis, quatenùs homini ambulanti adjunctæ unum cum eo corpus cõponunt; Moventur rotulæ etiam motu navigij in mari fluctuantis quatenùs adjunctæ sunt navigio; Insuper movetur motu maris quatenùs adjunctæ sunt mari; moventur deindè motu Terræ, quatenùs adjunctæ sunt Terræ, siquidem tota Terra moveatur; Moventur deniq; motu vorticis Terræ, quatenùs ei quoq; adjunctæ sunt, &c.
main_text.head: I.

p.i: Philosophia, quæ Cartesiana non est, ne unam de unâ re demonstrationem facere potest.

main_text.head: II.

p.i: Absque cognitione motus nulla est naturæ scientia.

main_text.head: III.

p.i: Ante Cartesium scivit nemo quid esset motus.

main_text.head: IV.

p.i: Pulvisculus in aëre volans gravior est totâ Terrâ.

main_text.head: V.

p.i: Si homo unum pedem extra Terram firmiter collocare

page.notes: The ornamental divider between the paragraph and COROLLARIA is a printer's fleuron, not transcribed. Heading "XXXV." is a section number. The catchword "collocare" is at the lower right.
